ud2.4:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud2.4:1.3: Then at that time the Fortunate One
ud2.4:1.4: was venerated, respected, revered, honoured, esteemed, and in receipt of robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal requisites to help when sick; also the Community of monks was venerated, respected, revered, honoured, esteemed, and in receipt of robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal requisites to help when sick.
ud2.4:1.5: But wanderers from other sects were not venerated, not respected, not revered, not honoured, not esteemed, nor were they in receipt of robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal requisites to help when sick.
ud2.4:1.6: Then those wanderers from other sects, being unable to bear the veneration of the Fortunate One and the Community of monks, after seeing the monks in the village or the wilderness, with vulgar and rough words scolded, abused, annoyed, and troubled them.
ud2.4:2.1: Then many monks went to the Fortunate One, and after going and worshipping the Fortunate One, they sat down on one side. While sat on one side those monks said this to the Fortunate One:
ud2.4:2.2: “At present, reverend Sir, the Fortunate One is venerated, respected, revered, honoured, esteemed, and in receipt of robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal requisites to help when sick;
ud2.4:2.3: also the Community of monks is venerated, respected, revered, honoured, esteemed, and in receipt of robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal requisites to help when sick.
ud2.4:2.4: But wanderers from other sects are not venerated, not respected, not revered, not honoured, not esteemed, nor are they in receipt of robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal requisites to help when sick.
ud2.4:2.5: Then those wanderers from other sects, reverend Sir, being unable to bear the veneration of the Fortunate One and the Community of monks, after seeing the monks in the village or the wilderness, with vulgar and rough words scold, abuse, annoy, and trouble them.”
ud2.4:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud2.4:4.1: “Affected by pleasure and pain in the village or wilderness,
ud2.4:4.2: you should certainly not consider it as due to oneself or another.
ud2.4:4.3: Contacts affect one with cleaving as condition,
ud2.4:4.4: How could contacts affect one without cleaving?”
